suggestionContent:
**sameRepository fallback can match a config on another instance**

The name-only match can hand the webhook to a config known to live on another instance when two servers share the same `group/project` path and numeric id, routing `WebhookContextService.getContext` to the wrong organization. Require `configHostsOf(config, repositoryId).length === 0` before a name match wins, and add a spec for two same-path projects on two hosts.
label: bug

suggestionContent:
**GitLab SSH clone URL drops configs and skips issue generation**

When `GitlabMapper.mapRepository` sets `url` to the SSH clone remote, `normalizeHost` returns a value no stored host equals, so `instanceConfigsForWebhook` drops every config and issues are silently skipped. Pass `gitlabWebhookSource(payload)` for the GitLab branch, as the handlers and `SavePullRequestUseCase` do.
label: bug

suggestionContent:
**Legacy-config test passes on the pre-fix revision, pinning nothing**

This input resolves to org-only with or without the new legacy-matching logic, so the case cannot catch a regression. Use a host-less legacy config listed beside a config storing another instance's host, with the payload naming a host no config matches, and assert the legacy config wins.

**Also found in:**
- `libs/platform/infrastructure/adapters/services/find-config-by-repository.spec.ts:72-82`
label: kody_rules

suggestionContent:
**Azure config lookup ignores the sending instance host**

Correlating by repository id and platform alone lets `findOne` return a config on another server that lists the same repository id, routing the event to the wrong workspace. Match configs whose listed repo URL or auth host equals `webhookHost`, keep host-less legacy configs, and drop the event when nothing on the sending instance matches.

**Also found in:**
- `libs/platform/infrastructure/adapters/services/bitbucket.service.ts:137-140`
- `libs/platform/application/use-cases/codeManagement/chatWithKodyFromGit.use-case.ts:1677-1683`
label: kody_rules

suggestionContent:
**Test passes even with the unscoped-lookup regression it should catch**

This case passes on the pre-fix revision: `findOne` resolves `undefined`, so the method returns `null` whether or not the lookup is scoped. Make the `findOne` mock resolve a config on the other server and assert `findOne` was not called, so an unscoped-lookup regression fails.
label: bug

suggestionContent:
**GitLab webhook config lookup drops repository-name fallback**

Without a fallback, a call with no `repositoryFullName` can never reach the same-repository match in `instanceConfigsForWebhook`, and `gitlabWebhookSource` yields undefined exactly when the payload has no parseable project URL, so the comment is dropped. Fall back to `params.repositoryFullName ?? params.repository.fullName ?? params.repository.name`, as Forgejo does.
label: bug

suggestionContent:
**GitLab regressions assert only mocked calls, not persisted data**

Mocked calls pin nothing about stored fields, so a regression that saves under the wrong organization or drops a lookup clause stays green. Run the use case against a real store, read the pull-request document back, and assert it landed under org-b/team-b with org-a unchanged.
label: kody_rules
